data.value: Unity calls Update or LateUpdate on a component once a frame while it is alive and enabled. This is the kind of work that tracks frame rate most directly - though how much it costs depends entirely on what the code inside does.
data.comment: Update, LateUpdate and Unity are names from the game engine and stay as they are.

data.name: Footprint_PhysicsEffect
data.value: FixedUpdate runs on the physics timestep - fifty times a second by default - and not once a frame. It can run several times in one frame or not at all in another, so its cost does not track your frame rate the way an Update does.
data.comment: FixedUpdate and Update are names from the game engine and stay as they are.

data.name: Footprint_GuiEffect
data.value: Unity calls OnGUI more than once a frame - a layout pass, then once per input event - and immediate-mode code typically allocates on each call, which adds garbage collection pressure. What it actually draws decides how much that matters.
data.comment: OnGUI and Unity are names from the game engine and stay as they are.

data.name: Footprint_ImageEffectEffect
data.value: OnRenderImage takes the rendered frame and writes a new one, for each camera the component is attached to. That work is done by the graphics card and scales with resolution rather than with processor speed.
data.comment: OnRenderImage is a name from the game engine and stays as it is.

data.value: OnPreRender and OnPostRender run either side of a camera drawing, once per camera per frame. They run on the processor rather than the graphics card, whatever the code inside them may go on to set up.
data.comment: OnPreRender and OnPostRender are names from the game engine and stay as they are.

data.name: Footprint_PatchesEffect
data.value: A patch class alters one of the game's own methods - usually a single one, though one class can target several, so this is a floor rather than a total. Where a patch sits is what decides its cost, and that is exactly what reading the files cannot establish: a patch on a method the game calls thousands of times a second is indistinguishable here from one on a menu button. Read this as how far the mod reaches, not as what it costs.
